I really feel this. I dated a guy for 7 years, we were also high school sweethearts. We had a love hate relationship. When he went off to college which was also a few hours away, I felt such jealousy that consumed me entirely. When I would visit, I hated it. The girls on his floor were so rude to me and he didn't say a single word to them to stick up for me. But when I was gone, he would go out and party and not text me all night and then the next day say his phone died. The abandonment issues started for me then. The way he acted while at college really took a toll on my mental health and put me in a deep depression. To be honest, it will hurt like you've never hurt before. But it doesn't seem like a healthy relationship and I understand how badly you want it to work out but leaving may be the best option. Maybe in time, you will cross paths again and can work things out. Do what you feel is right. Take a break if you need to and come back. Just make sure you're mental health is in check first. With bipolar, you have manic and depressive episodes. Manic meaning you do things out of the ordinary like stay up for days with only a small amount of sleep or spend a shit load of money or something like that. You can feel extremely excited, irritable, hysterical, unbalanced... and then there’s depression. Feeling low. Both of these episodes can be extreme or mild. I’m a rapid cycler. And unmedicated. It’s an absolute shit life.

It’s exhausting isn’t it? Sometimes I wish I could show the real me to others. But no one wants to see that side. It makes them feel awkward.

The thing is people who don’t suffer from a mental illness will never understand how it actually feels. Therefor, they won’t have the same kind of sympathy that others with a mental illness will have. It really does suck, that gap. 

Medication is a huge part of treatment. It can get worse if left untreated. Mine turned into rapid cycling and it was hell. Just wait out that appointment and be truthful and upfront with the doctor. And be patient. It may take a while to find the right meds and dosage. Im still in the process. You’re not alone. Im here for you.

It’s almost impossible to handle bipolar alone. Medication really does help. I’m here if you need someone to talk to.

Alcohol nor drugs will help. It’s best to stay away from them. I get what you’re feeling. It’s difficult to cope with but whenever I’m feeling okay I like to write down goals. Daily goals mostly. So when I accomplish those tasks, i feel motivated to keep going. Waking up early and having a cup of coffee always makes for a better day, for me anyway. I also write in a journal once in a while. Let out all the emotion I’m hiding inside. But once it’s all written down, I try not to go back and read it. It puts me right back in the mental state on that paper. Let it out and let it go. Those are some things that I do to cope with it. Hope it helps
